1	# audit-chain
2	
3	Per-tenant audit log where every entry is chained to its predecessor, so a reader can verify a tenant history offline and pinpoint the first broken index.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit append <tenant> --payload <json-file>
16	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit verify <tenant>
17	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit recover
18	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit rotate
19	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit compact [--max-segments N]
20	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit archive <archive-dir>
21	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit export <tenant> --start N --end M > proof.json
22	    python3 -m audit_chain verify-proof proof.json [--tenant T] [--start N] [--end M]
23	
24	`--path` is either a single JSON-lines log file or a segment store
25	(directory); the first `rotate` migrates an existing file into a store at the
26	same path. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` verification found a broken entry
27	(including a tampered cache, manifest or sealed window), `2` any other error
28	(missing file, bad/half-written line, corrupt chain, bad payload type,
29	illegal proof range, lock contention, path/permission errors). Error paths
30	print nothing. `verify-proof` never opens the log.
31	
32	## Public interface
33	
34	`audit_chain.Chain(path)` opens the log file.
35	- `append(tenant, payload) -> dict` appends and returns the stored entry.
36	- `entries(tenant) -> list[dict]` returns entries in insertion order.
37	- `verify(tenant) -> dict` re-derives the chain and reports the first bad index.
38	- `head(tenant) -> str | None` returns the newest digest.
39	- `export_range(tenant, start, end) -> dict` builds an offline proof for the
40	  half-open interval `[start, end)` (see below).
41	
42	Additional entry points:
43	- `recover() -> {"truncated_bytes": n}` truncates a half-written tail line
44	  left by a killed process; complete but broken records are never repaired.
45	- `rotate()` seals the active segment and starts a new one.
46	- `compact(max_segments=2) -> {"segments": n}` merges old segments.
47	- `archive(archive_dir) -> {"archived": n}` migrates every sealed segment
48	  to the caller-specified archive directory, online.
49	
50	`audit_chain.verify_proof(proof, *, tenant=None, start=None, end=None)`
51	verifies an exported proof with the public digest function alone; it never
52	touches the log.
53	
54	Two more offline entry points work purely on proof objects (no log):
55	- `audit_chain.combine_proofs(left, right) -> dict` splices two proofs of the
56	  same tenant whose intervals meet end-to-start (`left["end"] ==
57	  right["start"]`) into one ordinary proof covering the union
58	  `[left["start"], right["end"])`. It is associative, re-verifies both inputs
59	  and the result, and the combined proof checks out through `verify_proof`
60	  after the log itself has been compressed or deleted. A non-dict argument is
61	  `TypeError`; a side that is not a valid exporting proof or does not verify,
62	  or a tenant mismatch / gap / overlap / reversed order, is `ValueError`.
63	- `audit_chain.verify_proofs(proofs) -> list[dict]` verifies a batch and
64	  returns one verdict per proof, in input order, each with the same shape as
65	  the on-chain verdict. A tampered proof yields an `ok=False` verdict with the
66	  real global bad index without interrupting the rest. An empty list is
67	  `ValueError`; the argument or an element that is not a dict is `TypeError`.
68	
69	### Online archiving
70	
71	`archive(archive_dir)` moves every sealed segment out of the hot store
72	into the caller-specified archive directory while the log stays online.
73	The self-authenticating manifest records the archive location and keeps
74	each migrated segment's byte-window material, so later opens need no
75	extra arguments: append, query, verify, rotate, compact, recover and
76	export all work unchanged across the hot and archive tiers, per-tenant
77	indices stay continuous from zero, rotation order is untouched, and a
78	post-archive verify reports exactly the first bad index a pre-archive
79	verify would. Migrated segments no longer occupy the hot directory. The
80	migration is serialized with appends and merges by the same lock, so a
81	concurrent reader always sees one complete prefix and a writer is never
82	starved out; a process killed mid-migration reopens onto either the
83	pre-archive or the complete post-archive topology -- staged copies,
84	orphans and hot duplicates are reaped deterministically, and no segment
85	is ever half moved or left in both tiers. Archiving a damaged log, a
86	legacy unsegmented file, or a location that conflicts with the recorded
87	one raises `ValueError`.
88	
89	### Snapshot consistency
90	
91	`verify`, `entries` and `head` each run under a shared process lock and read
92	one fixed unit list in one ordered pass, while append/rotate/compact/recover
93	run under an exclusive lock. A single call therefore always observes one
94	complete prefix — the topology immediately before or immediately after a
95	rotation or merge — never mixed segments, a duplicated run or a skipped run.
96	
97	### Incremental, constant-read-amplification verification
98	
99	Concurrent appenders to one log are serialized by a cross-platform file lock
100	(`flock` on POSIX, `LockFileEx` on Windows), so records always link strictly
101	with continuous zero-based per-tenant indices. Each sealed segment keeps
102	byte-level verification material (size + sha256 per source segment, retained
103	through compaction). A repeat verify hashes only newly appended bytes plus a
104	small amount of sidecar material — never the whole file, and never a sealed
105	byte window on the hot path. The manifest is self-authenticating and the
106	verify cache is authenticated; tampering with the cache, the manifest or a
107	sealed window is reported as corruption (`ok=False`) with the real first bad
108	index rather than a pass. Tenants stay isolated: one tenant's damage never
109	changes another tenant's verdict.
110	
111	### Offline range proofs
112	
113	`export_range(tenant, start, end)` returns a self-contained proof for a
114	contiguous interval. It contains only the interval's chained records and the
115	strictly-increasing cross-segment window anchors (offset/size/sha256) needed
116	to attach them; no out-of-interval payload is included. An independent reader
117	recomputes every digest, checks predecessor links, indices, offsets and the
118	window chain using `verify_proof` (and the public digest) alone. Damage
119	outside the interval cannot affect its conclusion. Empty or reversed
120	intervals, non-integer or out-of-bounds ranges raise `ValueError`; a tenant
121	with no history returns a verifiable empty-history proof for `(0, 0)`.
122	
123	Two proofs exported from the same tenant can be joined with
124	`combine_proofs`: when their indices meet end-to-start the result is the same
125	kind of proof over the union, independently verifiable, and associating three
126	pieces pairwise gives the same conclusion as one proof over the whole range.
127	This holds with endpoints on segment boundaries, across segments merged by
128	compaction, and across the cross-segment window chain; it stays verifiable
129	after the log is compacted, corrupted or deleted. `verify_proofs` verifies
130	many proofs at once, one verdict each in order.
131	
132	### Export cost
133	
134	Exporting (and splicing, and batch verification) costs work proportional to
135	the interval, not to total history length. With a warm, authenticated verify
136	cache an export opens only the segment files that hold an interval record and
137	reads no others; records in sealed segments are anchored straight from the
138	signed manifest material, so sealed bytes are never hashed, and records in the
139	still-growing tail are anchored over small windows containing only the
140	interval's own lines. A never-verified or altered store transparently falls
141	back to a full ordered byte scan with identical conclusions.
142	
143	### Crash recovery
144	
145	Every commit is a temp-file write + fsync + atomic rename, and a merge
146	publishes its bytes before swapping the manifest and only removes old
147	segments afterwards. A process hard-killed in any window (partial write,
148	flush/fsync, segment rename, manifest replacement, old-segment deletion)
149	reopens onto either the old topology or the complete new one: a migration
150	backup is adopted, a staged directory / orphan segment / residual temp file
151	is reaped by the next writer, and a half-written tail line keeps its bad-line
152	semantics until `recover()` truncates it.
153	
154	## Tests
155	
156	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
157	
158	The suite includes a real-kill crash-injection matrix (separate processes
159	hard-killed at each commit window), concurrent snapshot-consistency stress,
160	tamper-evidence tests and offline-proof tests.
161	
162	## Limits
163	
164	Payloads must be JSON-serialisable.
165	No network service and no remote anchoring.
166

# audit-chain

Per-tenant audit log where every entry is chained to its predecessor, so a reader can verify a tenant history offline and pinpoint the first broken index.

## Requirements

Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install -e .

## Run

    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit append <tenant> --payload <json-file>
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit verify <tenant>
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit recover
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit rotate
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit compact [--max-segments N]
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit archive <archive-dir>
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit export <tenant> --start N --end M > proof.json

(directory); the first `rotate` migrates an existing file into a store at the
same path. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` verification found a broken entry
(including a tampered cache, manifest or sealed window), `2` any other error

illegal proof range, lock contention, path/permission errors). Error paths

  returns one verdict per proof, in input order, each with the same shape as
  the on-chain verdict. A tampered proof yields an `ok=False` verdict with the
  real global bad index without interrupting the rest. An empty list is

into the caller-specified archive directory while the log stays online.

each migrated segment's byte-window material, so later opens need no
extra arguments: append, query, verify, rotate, compact, recover and
export all work unchanged across the hot and archive tiers, per-tenant

migration is serialized with appends and merges by the same lock, so a
concurrent reader always sees one complete prefix and a writer is never
starved out; a process killed mid-migration reopens onto either the
pre-archive or the complete post-archive topology -- staged copies,
orphans and hot duplicates are reaped deterministically, and no segment
is ever half moved or left in both tiers. Archiving a damaged log, a
legacy unsegmented file, or a location that conflicts with the recorded
one raises `ValueError`.

### Snapshot consistency

`verify`, `entries` and `head` each run under a shared process lock and read
one fixed unit list in one ordered pass, while append/rotate/compact/recover
run under an exclusive lock. A single call therefore always observes one
complete prefix — the topology immediately before or immediately after a
rotation or merge — never mixed segments, a duplicated run or a skipped run.

### Incremental, constant-read-amplification verification

Concurrent appenders to one log are serialized by a cross-platform file lock
(`flock` on POSIX, `LockFileEx` on Windows), so records always link strictly
with continuous zero-based per-tenant indices. Each sealed segment keeps
byte-level verification material (size + sha256 per source segment, retained
through compaction). A repeat verify hashes only newly appended bytes plus a
small amount of sidecar material — never the whole file, and never a sealed
byte window on the hot path. The manifest is self-authenticating and the
verify cache is authenticated; tampering with the cache, the manifest or a
sealed window is reported as corruption (`ok=False`) with the real first bad
index rather than a pass. Tenants stay isolated: one tenant's damage never
changes another tenant's verdict.

### Offline range proofs

`export_range(tenant, start, end)` returns a self-contained proof for a
contiguous interval. It contains only the interval's chained records and the
strictly-increasing cross-segment window anchors (offset/size/sha256) needed
to attach them; no out-of-interval payload is included. An independent reader
recomputes every digest, checks predecessor links, indices, offsets and the
window chain using `verify_proof` (and the public digest) alone. Damage
outside the interval cannot affect its conclusion. Empty or reversed
intervals, non-integer or out-of-bounds ranges raise `ValueError`; a tenant
with no history returns a verifiable empty-history proof for `(0, 0)`.

Two proofs exported from the same tenant can be joined with
`combine_proofs`: when their indices meet end-to-start the result is the same
kind of proof over the union, independently verifiable, and associating three
pieces pairwise gives the same conclusion as one proof over the whole range.
This holds with endpoints on segment boundaries, across segments merged by
compaction, and across the cross-segment window chain; it stays verifiable
after the log is compacted, corrupted or deleted. `verify_proofs` verifies
many proofs at once, one verdict each in order.

### Export cost

Exporting (and splicing, and batch verification) costs work proportional to
the interval, not to total history length. With a warm, authenticated verify
cache an export opens only the segment files that hold an interval record and
reads no others; records in sealed segments are anchored straight from the
signed manifest material, so sealed bytes are never hashed, and records in the
still-growing tail are anchored over small windows containing only the
interval's own lines. A never-verified or altered store transparently falls
back to a full ordered byte scan with identical conclusions.

### Crash recovery

Every commit is a temp-file write + fsync + atomic rename, and a merge
publishes its bytes before swapping the manifest and only removes old
segments afterwards. A process hard-killed in any window (partial write,
flush/fsync, segment rename, manifest replacement, old-segment deletion)
reopens onto either the old topology or the complete new one: a migration
backup is adopted, a staged directory / orphan segment / residual temp file
is reaped by the next writer, and a half-written tail line keeps its bad-line
semantics until `recover()` truncates it.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

The suite includes a real-kill crash-injection matrix (separate processes
hard-killed at each commit window), concurrent snapshot-consistency stress,
tamper-evidence tests and offline-proof tests.

## Limits

Payloads must be JSON-serialisable.
No network service and no remote anchoring.

549	            if layout.kind == "file":
550	                self._migrate_file(layout)
551	            else:
552	                self._rotate_dir(layout)

554	    def _migrate_file(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
555	        path = layout.root
556	        raw = b""
557	        if os.path.exists(path):
558	            with open(path, "rb") as handle:
559	                raw = handle.read()
560	            # A crashed half-line must be recovered, not silently migrated.
561	            st.decode_records(raw)
562	
563	        parent = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
564	        staging = path + ".segstage"
565	        backup = path + ".pre-segment"
566	        if os.path.exists(backup):
567	            os.remove(backup)
568	        os.mkdir(staging)
569	        try:
570	            if raw:
571	                first = st.seg_name(st.FIRST_SEQ)
572	                second = st.seg_name(st.FIRST_SEQ + 1)
573	                self._write_bytes(staging, first, raw)
574	                self._write_bytes(staging, second, b"")
575	                manifest = {
576	                    "version": 1,
577	                    "active": second,
578	                    "segments": [
579	                        {
580	                            "name": first,
581	                            "sealed": True,
582	                            "parts": [
583	                                {
584	                                    "name": first,
585	                                    "size": len(raw),
586	                                    "sha256": _sha256(raw),
587	                                }
588	                            ],
589	                        },
590	                        {"name": second, "sealed": False, "parts": []},
591	                    ],
592	                }
593	            else:
594	                first = st.seg_name(st.FIRST_SEQ)
595	                self._write_bytes(staging, first, b"")
596	                manifest = st.default_manifest(first)
597	            st.save_manifest_at(staging, manifest)
598	            st.crash_point("migrate:after_staging")
599	
600	            # Keep the old data until the new store is in place: rename it
601	            # aside, publish the store, then drop the backup. Every kill in
602	            # between lands on one topology and is healed on next open.
603	            committed = False
604	            if os.path.exists(path):
605	                os.replace(path, backup)
606	                st.fsync_dir(parent)
607	            st.crash_point("migrate:after_backup_rename")
608	            try:
609	                os.replace(staging, path)
610	                st.fsync_dir(parent)
611	                committed = True
612	            finally:
613	                if not committed:
614	                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
615	                        os.replace(backup, path)
616	                        st.fsync_dir(parent)
617	            st.crash_point("migrate:after_publish")
618	            if os.path.exists(backup):
619	                os.remove(backup)
620	                st.fsync_dir(parent)
621	        except BaseException:
622	            # Roll the staging directory back out; the original file lives on
623	            # as the backup until the new store is fully published.
624	            if os.path.isdir(staging):
625	                for name in os.listdir(staging):
626	                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
627	                        os.unlink(os.path.join(staging, name))
628	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
629	                    os.rmdir(staging)
630	            raise
631	
632	        # The lock is topology-independent and stays put; the legacy sidecar
633	        # described the former single file, whereas the store's cache lives
634	        # inside the directory. Drop the stale one and warm the store's cache
635	        # from the bytes just migrated (mirrors _rotate_dir), so an export
636	        # right after the first rotation need not cold-scan the history.
637	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
638	            os.remove(layout.cache_path)
639	        new_layout = st.Layout(self.path, "dir")
640	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError, ValueError):
641	            self._walk(self._view(new_layout), new_layout)
642	
643	    def _rotate_dir(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
644	        units = self._view(layout)
645	        manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
646	        active_name = manifest["active"]
647	        active_unit = next(unit for unit in units if unit["name"] == active_name)
648	        active_manifest = next(
649	            segment for segment in manifest["segments"] if segment["name"] == active_name
650	        )
651	        size = os.path.getsize(active_unit["path"])
652	        if size == 0:
653	            return
654	
655	        # Walk first so a corrupt active segment cannot be sealed away.
656	        states, entries = self._walk(units, layout)
657	        for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
658	            if bad != -1:
659	                raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")
660	
661	        # Freeze the active bytes as verification material: keep windows the
662	        # segment already preserved (e.g. from a fold-to-one compaction) and
663	        # add one window for the bytes appended after them.
664	        with open(active_unit["path"], "rb") as handle:
665	            active_bytes = handle.read()
666	        sealed_prefix = sum(part["size"] for part in active_manifest["parts"])
667	        seal_parts = [dict(part) for part in active_manifest["parts"]]
668	        if seal_parts and not st.verify_prefix_windows(
669	            active_unit["path"], seal_parts
670	        ):
671	            raise ValueError("corrupt audit segment")
672	        if len(active_bytes) > sealed_prefix:
673	            seal_parts.append(
674	                {
675	                    "name": active_name,
676	                    "size": len(active_bytes) - sealed_prefix,
677	                    "sha256": _sha256(active_bytes[sealed_prefix:]),
678	                }
679	            )
680	        entries[active_name]["parts"] = [dict(part) for part in seal_parts]
681	        for segment in manifest["segments"]:
682	            if segment["name"] == active_name:
683	                segment["sealed"] = True
684	                segment["parts"] = seal_parts
685	        next_seq = max(st.seg_seq(s["name"]) for s in manifest["segments"]) + 1
686	        new_active = st.seg_name(next_seq)
687	        # The new segment is an unreferenced orphan until the manifest commit
688	        # names it; a kill in this window simply has it garbage-collected and
689	        # the old topology remains authoritative.
690	        self._write_bytes(layout.root, new_active, b"")
691	        st.crash_point("rotate:before_manifest")
692	        manifest["segments"].append(
693	            {"name": new_active, "sealed": False, "parts": []}
694	        )
695	        manifest["active"] = new_active
696	        st.save_manifest(layout, manifest)
697	        st.crash_point("rotate:after_manifest")
698	        st.save_cache(layout, entries)
699	
700	    def compact(self, max_segments: int = _DEFAULT_MAX_SEGMENTS) -> dict:
701	        """Merge old sealed segments while keeping each one's material.
702	
703	        The log is folded until at most ``max_segments`` segments remain
704	        (the active segment counts). Each merge concatenates the source
705	        bytes and retains their ordered (size, sha256) windows, so every
706	        source segment's verification material survives compression and the
707	        global insertion order is unchanged.
708	
709	        Merged bytes are staged in a temp file and renamed before the
710	        atomic manifest commit; the old segments are removed only after the
711	        commit. A kill at any point therefore leaves the old topology or
712	        the complete new topology plus unreferenced files reaped on reopen.
713	        """
714	        if max_segments < 1:
715	            raise ValueError("max_segments must be >= 1")
716	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
717	            if layout.kind != "dir":
718	                raise ValueError("log is not segmented; call rotate() first")
719	            units = self._view(layout)
720	
721	            # Never fold a damaged log.
722	            states, _ = self._walk(units, layout)
723	            for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
724	                if bad != -1:
725	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")
726	
727	            manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
728	            cache = st.load_cache(layout)
729	            cache_segments = {} if cache is None else dict(cache["segments"])
730	
731	            if max_segments == 1 and len(manifest["segments"]) > 1:
732	                removed = self._merge_all(layout, manifest, cache_segments)
733	            else:
734	                removed: list[dict] = []
735	                while len(manifest["segments"]) > max_segments:
736	                    removed += self._merge_pair(layout, manifest, cache_segments)
737	
738	            if removed:
739	                # Commit the new topology first; the now-unreferenced
740	                # sources are removed after the durable manifest swap and
741	                # otherwise garbage collected on the next open, so a crash
742	                # never loses data and never exposes a mixed topology.
743	                st.save_manifest(layout, manifest)
744	                st.crash_point("compact:after_manifest")
745	                st.save_cache(layout, cache_segments)
746	                for source in removed:
747	                    with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
748	                        os.remove(self._segment_path(layout, manifest, source))
749	                    st.crash_point("compact:during_delete")
750	                st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
751	                st.crash_point("compact:after_delete")
752	            count = len(manifest["segments"])
753	        return {"segments": count}
754

759	    def archive(self, archive_dir: str) -> dict:
760	        """Migrate every sealed segment to ``archive_dir``, online.
761	
762	        The archive location is caller-specified and recorded in the
763	        self-authenticating manifest, so every later open of this store
764	        resolves archived segments across the two tiers with no extra
765	        arguments. Migrated segments keep their names, window material and
766	        position in the manifest: per-tenant indices, rotation order,
767	        verdicts and exported proofs are exactly what they were before the
768	        move, and the hot directory no longer holds the migrated bytes.
769	
770	        The migration is online and crash-safe. It runs under the same
771	        exclusive lock as append/rotate/compact, so a concurrent caller
772	        always observes one complete prefix -- the pre-archive or the
773	        post-archive topology, never a mix. The location is committed
774	        first, then every segment is copied through a temp file + fsync +
775	        atomic rename, then a second manifest commit marks the segments
776	        archived, and only then are the hot copies removed. A process
777	        killed in any window reopens onto one complete topology: staged
778	        copies, orphans and hot duplicates are reaped deterministically,
779	        and no segment is ever lost or left in both tiers.
780	
781	        Returns ``{"archived": n}`` -- the number of segments this call
782	        migrated (zero when every sealed segment is already archived).
783	        Raises ``ValueError`` on a legacy file layout (rotate first), a
784	        corrupt chain, an archive directory inside the store itself, or a
785	        different location than an earlier archive call recorded.
786	        """
787	        dest = os.path.abspath(os.fspath(archive_dir))
788	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
789	            if layout.kind != "dir":
790	                raise ValueError("log is not segmented; call rotate() first")
791	            if os.path.normpath(dest) == os.path.normpath(
792	                os.path.abspath(layout.root)
793	            ):
794	                raise ValueError("archive directory must differ from the store")
795	            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(dest, st.MANIFEST_NAME)):
796	                raise ValueError("archive directory is itself a segment store")
797	            units = self._view(layout)
798	            manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
799	
800	            # Never migrate a damaged log.
801	            states, _ = self._walk(units, layout)
802	            for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
803	                if bad != -1:
804	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")
805	
806	            recorded = manifest.get("archive")
807	            if recorded is not None and os.path.normpath(recorded) != os.path.normpath(
808	                dest
809	            ):
810	                raise ValueError("log already archives to a different location")
811	
812	            targets = [
813	                segment
814	                for segment in manifest["segments"]
815	                if segment["sealed"] and not segment.get("archived")
816	            ]
817	            if not targets:
818	                return {"archived": 0}
819	
820	            os.makedirs(dest, exist_ok=True)
821	            # Raise the in-flight marker before the first commit: until the
822	            # migration is fully settled the marker tells every reopening
823	            # reader/writer to finish the tier housekeeping first, so a
824	            # kill anywhere in the middle never reopens onto copies kept in
825	            # both tiers.
826	            marker = os.path.join(layout.root, _ARCHIVE_MARKER)
827	            fd = os.open(
828	                marker, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC | _O_BINARY, 0o600
829	            )
830	            os.close(fd)
831	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
832	            st.crash_point("archive:after_marker")
833	            if recorded is None:
834	                # Commit the location first: a kill during the copies then
835	                # still reopens knowing where staged bytes may lie, and the
836	                # reaper settles the tree back onto the hot-only topology.
837	                manifest["archive"] = dest
838	                st.save_manifest(layout, manifest)
839	                st.crash_point("archive:after_location")
840	
841	            for segment in targets:
842	                source = layout.segment_path(segment["name"])
843	                # The pre-walk may have vouched for this segment from the
844	                # authenticated cache alone; re-check its frozen windows
845	                # against the bytes before they become the only copy.
846	                if not st.verify_windows(source, segment["parts"]):
847	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit segment")
848	                with open(source, "rb") as handle:
849	                    raw = handle.read()
850	                self._publish_bytes(dest, segment["name"], raw, phase="archive", kind="copy")
851	                st.crash_point("archive:after_copy")
852	
853	            migrated = {segment["name"] for segment in targets}
854	            for segment in manifest["segments"]:
855	                if segment["name"] in migrated:
856	                    segment["archived"] = True
857	            st.save_manifest(layout, manifest)
858	            st.crash_point("archive:after_manifest")
859	
860	            # Keep the verify cache warm across the move: the bytes are
861	            # identical, only each migrated segment's stat identity changed.
862	            cache = st.load_cache(layout)
863	            if cache is not None:
864	                cached_segments = cache["segments"]
865	                changed = False
866	                for name in migrated:
867	                    entry = cached_segments.get(name)
868	                    if entry is not None:
869	                        new_stat = os.stat(os.path.join(dest, name))
870	                        entry["size"] = new_stat.st_size
871	                        entry["mtime_ns"] = new_stat.st_mtime_ns
872	                        entry["ctime_ns"] = new_stat.st_ctime_ns
873	                        changed = True
874	                if changed:
875	                    st.save_cache(layout, cached_segments)
876	
877	            # The post-archive topology is durable; the hot copies are now
878	            # unreferenced and their removal is completed (or reaped on the
879	            # next open) without ever exposing a mixed topology.
880	            for name in migrated:
881	                with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
882	                    os.remove(layout.segment_path(name))
883	                st.crash_point("archive:during_delete")
884	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
885	            # Settled: lower the in-flight marker last of all.
886	            with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
887	                os.remove(marker)
888	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
889	            st.crash_point("archive:after_delete")
890	        return {"archived": len(migrated)}
891	
892	    def _gc_segments(self, layout: st.Layout, manifest: dict) -> None:
893	        """Remove segment files not referenced by the committed manifest."""
894	        referenced = {segment["name"] for segment in manifest["segments"]}
895	        changed = False
896	        for name in os.listdir(layout.root):
897	            if st.seg_seq(name) is not None and name not in referenced:
898	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
899	                    os.remove(layout.segment_path(name))
900	                    changed = True
901	        if changed:
902	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)

904	    def _gc_archive(self, layout: st.Layout, manifest: dict) -> None:
905	        """Settle an archived store onto exactly one topology.
906	
907	        A migration killed after its manifest commit leaves hot duplicates
908	        of archived segments; one killed before it leaves copied-but-
909	        unreferenced segments (or staging temp files) in the archive
910	        directory. Both are removed here so a reopened store never keeps
911	        copies of one segment in the two tiers.
912	        """
913	        archive_dir = manifest.get("archive")
914	        if not archive_dir:
915	            return
916	        changed = False
917	        for segment in manifest["segments"]:
918	            if not segment.get("archived"):
919	                continue
920	            hot = layout.segment_path(segment["name"])
921	            if os.path.exists(hot):
922	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
923	                    os.remove(hot)
924	                    changed = True
925	        if changed:
926	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
927	        if not os.path.isdir(archive_dir):
928	            return
929	        archived = {
930	            segment["name"] for segment in manifest["segments"] if segment.get("archived")
931	        }
932	        changed = False
933	        for name in os.listdir(archive_dir):
934	            # The archive tier holds exactly the segments the committed
935	            # manifest marks archived; any other segment file here is a
936	            # staged copy or merge orphan whose authoritative bytes live
937	            # in the hot tier.
938	            if (st.seg_seq(name) is not None and name not in archived) or (
939	                name.startswith(".") and name.endswith(".tmp")
940	            ):
941	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
942	                    os.remove(os.path.join(archive_dir, name))
943	                    changed = True
944	        if changed:
945	            st.fsync_dir(archive_dir)

947	    def _publish_bytes(
948	        self,
949	        directory: str,
950	        name: str,
951	        raw: bytes,
952	        *,
953	        phase: str = "compact",
954	        kind: str = "merge",
955	    ) -> str:
956	        """Stage ``raw`` in a temp file and rename it to ``directory/name``."""
957	        target = os.path.join(directory, name)
958	        tmp_path = os.path.join(directory, st._tmp_name_for(name))
959	        try:
960	            fd = os.open(
961	                tmp_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC | _O_BINARY, 0o600
962	            )
963	            try:
964	                _write_all(fd, raw)
965	                st.crash_point(f"{phase}:before_{kind}_fsync")
966	                os.fsync(fd)
967	            finally:
968	                os.close(fd)
969	            st.crash_point(f"{phase}:after_{kind}_write")
970	            os.replace(tmp_path, target)
971	            st.fsync_dir(directory)
972	            st.crash_point(f"{phase}:after_{kind}_rename")
973	        except BaseException:
974	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
975	                os.remove(tmp_path)
976	            raise
977	        return target

979	    def _merge_all(
980	        self, layout: st.Layout, manifest: dict, cache_segments: dict
981	    ) -> list[dict]:
982	        """Fold every segment, active included, into one active segment."""
983	        sources = manifest["segments"]
984	        merged, parts, carried = self._compose(layout, manifest, sources, cache_segments)
985	        name = st.seg_name(max(st.seg_seq(s["name"]) for s in sources) + 1)
986	        # The active segment always stays in the hot tier.
987	        target = self._publish_bytes(layout.root, name, merged)
988	        for source in sources:
989	            cache_segments.pop(source["name"], None)
990	        if carried is not None:
991	            cache_segments[name] = _cache_entry(
992	                carried["records"],
993	                os.stat(target),
994	                parts,
995	                _states_from(carried),
996	                _fold_of_bytes(merged),
997	            )
998	        manifest["segments"] = [
999	            {"name": name, "sealed": False, "parts": parts}
1000	        ]
1001	        manifest["active"] = name
1002	        return list(sources)
1003	
1004	    def _merge_pair(
1005	        self, layout: st.Layout, manifest: dict, cache_segments: dict
1006	    ) -> list[dict]:
1007	        """Merge the two oldest segments into one new sealed segment."""
1008	        sources = manifest["segments"][:2]
1009	        merged, parts, carried = self._compose(layout, manifest, sources, cache_segments)
1010	        name = st.seg_name(
1011	            max(st.seg_seq(s["name"]) for s in manifest["segments"]) + 1
1012	        )
1013	        # A merge of exclusively archived sources stays in the archive tier;
1014	        # anything else is published hot.
1015	        to_archive = all(source.get("archived") for source in sources)
1016	        directory = manifest["archive"] if to_archive else layout.root
1017	        target = self._publish_bytes(directory, name, merged)
1018	        merged_segment = {"name": name, "sealed": True, "parts": parts}
1019	        if to_archive:
1020	            merged_segment["archived"] = True
1021	        manifest["segments"] = [merged_segment] + manifest["segments"][2:]
1022	        for source in sources:
1023	            cache_segments.pop(source["name"], None)
1024	        if carried is not None:
1025	            cache_segments[name] = _cache_entry(
1026	                carried["records"],
1027	                os.stat(target),
1028	                parts,
1029	                _states_from(carried),
1030	                _fold_of_bytes(merged),
1031	            )
1032	        return list(sources)

1034	    def _compose(
1035	        self,
1036	        layout: st.Layout,
1037	        manifest: dict,
1038	        sources: list[dict],
1039	        cache_segments: dict,
1040	    ) -> tuple[bytes, list[dict], Optional[dict]]:
1041	        """Concatenate source bytes and windows, carrying warm cached states."""
1042	        chunks: list[bytes] = []
1043	        parts: list[dict] = []
1044	        for source in sources:
1045	            path = self._segment_path(layout, manifest, source)
1046	            with open(path, "rb") as handle:
1047	                data = handle.read()
1048	            if source["sealed"]:
1049	                windows = source["parts"]
1050	                if len(data) != sum(w["size"] for w in windows) or not st.verify_windows(
1051	                    path, windows
1052	                ):
1053	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit segment")
1054	            else:
1055	                # The active segment carries no preserved byte windows;
1056	                # freeze one full-content window for it now (read once).
1057	                windows = [
1058	                    {
1059	                        "name": source["name"],
1060	                        "size": len(data),
1061	                        "sha256": _sha256(data),
1062	                    }
1063	                ]
1064	            chunks.append(data)
1065	            parts.extend(dict(part) for part in windows)
1066	
1067	        # Cache entries hold cumulative per-tenant states, so after the
1068	        # sources in order the last cached entry describes the whole merge.
1069	        carried: Optional[dict] = None
1070	        for source in sources:
1071	            cached = cache_segments.get(source["name"])
1072	            if cached is None:
1073	                carried = None
1074	                break
1075	            carried = {
1076	                "records": cached["records"],
1077	                "tenants": {
1078	                    tenant: list(state) for tenant, state in cached["tenants"].items()
1079	                },
1080	            }
1081	        return b"".join(chunks), parts, carried

1085	    # Incremental verification walk
1086	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1087	
1088	    def _walk(
1089	        self,
1090	        units: list[dict],
1091	        layout: st.Layout,
1092	        *,
1093	        ignore_cache: bool = False,
1094	        persist: bool = True,
1095	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, int, int]], dict]:
1096	        """Walk every unit in order, reusing authenticated cached prefixes.
1097	
1098	        Returns ``(states, entries)``: states maps tenant to
1099	        ``(count, head_digest, first_bad)``; entries maps unit name to its
1100	        cache entry. Cost model:
1101	
1102	        * a unit unchanged since caching adopts the cached states with no
1103	          record reads or digest work -- the active unit is stat-guarded and
1104	          a sealed unit is guarded by its preserved window material, so no
1105	          sealed byte is hashed on the hot path;
1106	        * a grown active/legacy unit parses and chains only the appended
1107	          suffix, so a ten-thousand-entry re-verify never rehashes the file;
1108	        * a sealed segment is authenticated by its preserved byte windows
1109	          (merged segments keep one window per source segment), and damaged
1110	          windows are attributed to the tenants whose records they hold, so
1111	          one tenant's corruption never changes another tenant's verdict

1273	    @staticmethod
1274	    def _adopt_states(states: dict[str, list], entry: dict) -> None:
1275	        for tenant, state in entry["tenants"].items():
1276	            count, digest, bad = state

1287	    @staticmethod
1288	    def _stat_fresh(entry: dict, stat: os.stat_result, *, exact: bool = True) -> bool:
1289	        # size + mtime identify an unchanged append-only file; ctime (which
1290	        # utimes cannot restore) exposes a same-size content rewrite. The
1291	        # growth branch only needs size-growth + unchanged ctime.
1292	        if entry["ctime_ns"] != stat.st_ctime_ns:
1293	            return False
1294	        if not exact:
1295	            return entry["size"] <= stat.st_size
1296	        return (
1297	            entry["size"] == stat.st_size
1298	            and entry["mtime_ns"] == stat.st_mtime_ns
1299	        )

1301	    @staticmethod
1302	    def _entry_fresh(entry: dict, stat: os.stat_result, unit: dict) -> bool:
1303	        """Hot-path freshness with constant read amplification.
1304	
1305	        The size + mtime + ctime guard identifies an unchanged append-only
1306	        file (ctime exposes a same-size content rewrite and cannot be
1307	        restored). In addition, whenever the unit carries preserved byte
1308	        windows -- always for a sealed unit, and for an active unit after a
1309	        fold-to-one compaction -- the manifest's window material must match
1310	        what the cache authenticated, so an edited manifest window forces
1311	        the cold path and is reported as corruption, without a single sealed
1312	        byte being hashed on the ordinary path.
1313	        """
1314	        if not Chain._stat_fresh(entry, stat):
1315	            return False
1316	        cached_parts = entry.get("parts", [])
1317	        if unit["sealed"] or cached_parts or unit["parts"]:
1318	            return cached_parts == unit["parts"]
1319	        return True

1321	    def _walk_bytes(
1322	        self, unit: dict, states: dict[str, list]
1323	    ) -> tuple[int, list[dict], dict, str]:
1324	        """Parse and chain one unit's bytes.
1325	
1326	        Returns ``(record_count, cache_parts, failed_tenants, fold)`` where
1327	        ``failed_tenants`` maps each tenant with a record in a
1328	        content-hash-failed window to that record's global index, and
1329	        ``fold`` is the extendable byte fingerprint of the unit's complete
1330	        lines.
1331	
1332	        Content tampering normally breaks the victim's digest chain, which
1333	        attributes ``first_bad`` precisely and leaves tenants with no record
1334	        in the damaged window untouched. The window hash is an independent
1335	        tripwire: it only needs to act when the attacker also recomputed
1336	        digests (a clean-looking but rewritten log).
1337	        """
1338	        path = unit["path"]
1339	        windows = unit["parts"]
1340	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
1341	            raw = handle.read()
1342	
1343	        failed: set[int] = set()
1344	        window_ends: list[int] = []
1345	        if windows:
1346	            if unit["sealed"] and len(raw) != sum(
1347	                window["size"] for window in windows
1348	            ):
1349	                failed.update(range(len(windows)))
1350	            elif not st.verify_prefix_windows(path, windows):
1351	                failed.update(range(len(windows)))
1352	            running = 0
1353	            for window in windows:
1354	                running += window["size"]
1355	                window_ends.append(running)
1356	
1357	        try:
1358	            text = raw.decode(_ENCODING)
1359	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
1360	            raise ValueError("malformed audit record") from exc
1361	        lines = rec.split_records(text)
1362	
1363	        first_index: dict[str, int] = {}
1364	        win_index = 0
1365	        pos = 0
1366	        for line in lines:
1367	            length = len((line + "\n").encode(_ENCODING))
1368	            start, end = pos, pos + length
1369	            pos = end
1370	            while win_index < len(window_ends) and start >= window_ends[win_index]:
1371	                win_index += 1
1372	            past_end = win_index >= len(window_ends)
1373	            crosses = not past_end and end > window_ends[win_index]
1374	            window_failed = not past_end and win_index in failed
1375	
1376	            record = rec.parse_line(line)
1377	            tenant = record["tenant"]
1378	            count, head, bad = states.get(tenant, [0, "", -1])
1379	            if window_failed:
1380	                first_index.setdefault(tenant, count)
1381	            if crosses:
1382	                # Windows only ever concatenate whole lines, so a record may
1383	                # never straddle a window boundary.
1384	                if bad == -1:
1385	                    bad = count
1386	            if unit["sealed"] and past_end and bad == -1:
1387	                # Bytes appended past a sealed segment's frozen material.
1388	                bad = count
1389	            recomputed = rec.digest(record["prev"], record["payload"])
1390	            if record["prev"] != head or record["digest"] != recomputed:
1391	                if bad == -1:
1392	                    bad = count
1393	            states[tenant] = [count + 1, record["digest"], bad]
1394	
1395	        # Sealed units carry their full window material; an active unit
1396	        # carries preserved *prefix* windows after a fold-to-one compaction.
1397	        # Both are retained in the cache so the hot-path freshness guard
1398	        # compares the manifest's window material for either kind.
1399	        parts = [dict(part) for part in windows]
1400	        # split_records guaranteed raw ends in a terminator, so this folds
1401	        # every complete line exactly as the continuation branch will.
1402	        fold = _fold_of_bytes(raw)
1403	        return len(lines), parts, first_index, fold

1405	    def _apply_records(self, records: list[dict], states: dict[str,list]) -> None:
1406	        for record in records:
1407	            tenant = record["tenant"]
1408	            count, head, bad = states.get(tenant, [0, "", -1])
1409	            recomputed = rec.digest(record["prev"], record["payload"])
1410	            if record["prev"] != head or record["digest"] != recomputed:
1411	                if bad == -1:
1412	                    bad = count
1413	            states[tenant] = [count + 1, record["digest"], bad]

1419	    def export_range(self, tenant: str, start: int, end: int) -> dict:
1420	        """Build an offline proof for tenant records ``[start, end)``.
1421	
1422	        The proof contains only the interval's chained records and the
1423	        window anchors (ordered, strictly increasing windows) needed to
1424	        attach the interval to the prefix and confirm it is contiguous. No
1425	        payload outside the interval is included. An independent reader can
1426	        check it with :func:`audit_chain.proof.verify_proof` and the public
1427	        digest function alone.
1428	
1429	        Illegal, reversed, empty or out-of-range intervals raise
1430	        ``ValueError``; for a tenant with no history the empty-history
1431	        conclusion ``(0, 0)`` is the only interval accepted.
1432	        """
1433	        from . import proof as pf
1434	
1435	        if (
1436	            not isinstance(start, int)
1437	            or not isinstance(end, int)
1438	            or isinstance(start, bool)
1439	            or isinstance(end, bool)
1440	        ):
1441	            raise ValueError("range bounds must be integers")
1442	        if start < 0 or end < 0:
1443	            raise ValueError("range bounds must be non-negative")
1444	        if end < start:
1445	            raise ValueError("range is reversed: start must be <= end")
1446	
1447	        with self._locked(exclusive=False) as layout:
1448	            if layout.kind == "file" and not os.path.exists(layout.root):
1449	                # A log that was never created implies an empty history for
1450	                # every tenant; only the (0, 0) empty-history conclusion is
1451	                # in bounds.
1452	                if (start, end) == (0, 0):
1453	                    return pf.empty_proof(tenant)
1454	                raise ValueError("range is out of bounds for an empty history")
1455	            units = self._snapshot_units(layout, tolerate_metadata=True)
1456	            # Fast path: an authentic warm cache states each unit's
1457	            # cumulative tenant counts, so only units holding interval bytes
1458	            # are opened. With no trustworthy guide (never-verified log,
1459	            # grown active unit, edited bytes or metadata) fall back to the
1460	            # full ordered byte scan.
1461	            guide = self._export_guide(units, layout, tenant)
1462	            if guide is not None:
1463	                material = self._collect_range_bounded(
1464	                    units, tenant, start, end, guide
1465	                )
1466	            else:
1467	                material = self._collect_range(units, tenant, start, end)
1468	        return pf.build_proof(material)

1482	    def _collect_range(
1483	        self, units: list[dict], tenant: str, start: int, end: int
1484	    ) -> dict:
1485	        """One ordered snapshot scan collecting interval material.
1486	
1487	        Windows are numbered with one strictly increasing global sequence
1488	        across all units, so the proof carries an explicit cross-segment
1489	        window chain. Only records of ``tenant`` are parsed; malformed lines
1490	        and a trailing half line outside the interval are skipped, so damage
1491	        outside the interval cannot change its conclusion.
1492	        """
1493	        buckets: dict[int, list[tuple[int, int, dict]]] = {}
1494	        anchors: dict[int, dict] = {}
1495	        predecessor: Optional[str] = None
1496	        count = 0
1497	        global_seq = 0
1498	
1499	        for unit in units:
1500	            try:
1501	                with open(unit["path"], "rb") as handle:
1502	                    raw = handle.read()
1503	            except FileNotFoundError:
1504	                if not unit["sealed"]:
1505	                    continue
1506	                raise
1507	
1508	            parts = unit["parts"]
1509	            window_ends: list[int] = []
1510	            running = 0
1511	            for part in parts:
1512	                running += part["size"]
1513	                window_ends.append(running)
1514	                anchors[global_seq + len(window_ends) - 1] = {
1515	                    "name": part["name"],
1516	                    "size": part["size"],
1517	                    "sha256": part["sha256"],
1518	                }
1519	            tail_offset = running
1520	            tail_seq = global_seq + len(parts)
1521	            if len(raw) > tail_offset:
1522	                anchors[tail_seq] = {
1523	                    "name": unit["name"],
1524	                    "size": len(raw) - tail_offset,
1525	                    "sha256": _sha256(raw[tail_offset:]),
1526	                }
1527	            elif not parts:
1528	                # Legacy/active unit with no preserved material: its whole
1529	                # bytes are one implicit window.
1530	                anchors[tail_seq] = {
1531	                    "name": unit["name"],
1532	                    "size": len(raw),
1533	                    "sha256": _sha256(raw),
1534	                }
1535	
1536	            # Whole-line scan: a piece after the final newline is a crashed
1537	            # half line -- never a record, and irrelevant when out of range.
1538	            pos = 0
1539	            for line_raw in raw.split(b"\n")[:-1]:
1540	                line_start = pos
1541	                line_end = pos + len(line_raw) + 1
1542	                pos = line_end
1543	                try:
1544	                    record = st.decode_records(line_raw + b"\n")[0]
1545	                except ValueError:
1546	                    continue
1547	                if record["tenant"] != tenant:
1548	                    continue
1549	                if count == start:
1550	                    predecessor = record["prev"]
1551	                win_index = 0
1552	                while win_index < len(window_ends) and line_start >= window_ends[win_index]:
1553	                    win_index += 1
1554	                if win_index < len(window_ends):
1555	                    seq = global_seq + win_index
1556	                    window_start = window_ends[win_index - 1] if win_index else 0
1557	                else:
1558	                    seq = tail_seq
1559	                    window_start = tail_offset
1560	                if start <= count < end:
1561	                    buckets.setdefault(seq, []).append(
1562	                        (count, line_start - window_start, record)
1563	                    )
1564	                count += 1
1565	
1566	            global_seq += len(parts) + (1 if len(raw) > tail_offset or not parts else 0)
1567	
1568	        if count == 0:
1569	            if (start, end) == (0, 0):
1570	                return {
1571	                    "tenant": tenant,
1572	                    "start": 0,
1573	                    "end": 0,
1574	                    "count": 0,
1575	                    "prev": "",
1576	                    "anchors": {},
1577	                    "buckets": [],
1578	                }
1579	            raise ValueError("range is out of bounds for an empty history")
1580	        if start == end:
1581	            raise ValueError("range must be a non-empty interval")
1582	        if start >= count or end > count:
1583	            raise ValueError("range is out of bounds")
1584	
1585	        return {
1586	            "tenant": tenant,
1587	            "start": start,
1588	            "end": end,
1589	            "count": count,
1590	            "prev": predecessor if predecessor is not None else "",
1591	            "anchors": anchors,
1592	            "buckets": [
1593	                {"seq": seq, "records": records}
1594	                for seq, records in sorted(buckets.items())
1595	            ],
1596	        }

1602	    def _export_guide(
1603	        self, units: list[dict], layout: st.Layout, tenant: str
1604	    ) -> Optional[list[int]]:
1605	        """Each unit's cumulative tenant record count, or None when cold.
1606	
1607	        The verify cache is signed and a unit is adopted only when the exact
1608	        stat guard and its preserved-window material both match, so a
1609	        rewritten prefix, a same-size edit, a shrunk file, a grown active
1610	        unit or an edited manifest window all force the full byte scan
1611	        instead of trusting a guide that no longer matches the bytes.
1612	        """
1613	        try:
1614	            cache = st.load_cache(layout)
1615	        except st.AuditMetadataError:
1616	            return None
1617	        if cache is None or len(cache["segments"]) != len(units):
1618	            return None
1619	
1620	        counts: list[int] = []
1621	        for unit in units:
1622	            entry = cache["segments"].get(unit["name"])
1623	            if entry is None:
1624	                return None
1625	            try:
1626	                stat = os.stat(unit["path"])
1627	            except FileNotFoundError:
1628	                if not unit["sealed"]:
1629	                    return None
1630	                raise
1631	            if not self._entry_fresh(entry, stat, unit):
1632	                return None
1633	            state = entry["tenants"].get(tenant)
1634	            counts.append(state[0] if state is not None else 0)
1635	        return counts

1637	    def _collect_range_bounded(
1638	        self,
1639	        units: list[dict],
1640	        tenant: str,
1641	        start: int,
1642	        end: int,
1643	        counts: list[int],

1645	        """Collect interval material opening only covering units.

1648	        preserved sealed window is anchored by that window's manifest
1649	        material, so no sealed byte is hashed; records in the still-growing
1650	        un-preserved tail of an active/legacy unit are grouped into small
1651	        windows that contain only the interval's own consecutive lines, so
1652	        digest work tracks the interval rather than the unit. Total cost
1653	        therefore grows with the interval and the (bounded) covering units,
1654	        never with overall history length: non-covering units are never
1655	        opened and their sealed windows contribute no reads or hashes.
1656	        """
1657	        total = counts[-1]
1658	        if total == 0:
1659	            if (start, end) == (0, 0):
1660	                return {
1661	                    "tenant": tenant,
1662	                    "start": 0,
1663	                    "end": 0,
1664	                    "count": 0,
1665	                    "prev": "",
1666	                    "anchors": {},
1667	                    "buckets": [],
1668	                }
1669	            raise ValueError("range is out of bounds for an empty history")
1670	        if start == end:

"""Per-tenant hash-chained audit log.

Every entry stores the digest of its predecessor, so a tenant's history can
be walked offline and the first tampered index pinpointed. Tenants are
independent chains that share one physical log.

The original single JSON-lines file is extended without changing its
semantics:

* concurrent appenders to the same log are serialized by a process-shared,
  cross-platform file lock, so interlocked writes still link strictly;
* every read (``verify``/``entries``/``head``) takes a snapshot under a
  shared lock: a single call always sees one complete prefix -- the old
  topology or the new one around a rotation, merge or recovery -- never a
  mix of segments, a duplicate run or a skipped run;
* the log can be rotated into ordered segment files and compacted, with
  every source segment's verification material (byte size + sha256)
  retained through merges, committed by an atomic, self-authenticating
  manifest replacement; merged bytes are published through a temp file and
  rename, so every crash window lands on the old or the new topology;
* sealed segments can be migrated online into a caller-specified archive
  directory (cold tier): the signed manifest records the archive location
  and keeps every migrated segment's window material, so append, query,
  verify, rotate, compact, recover and export all work unchanged across
  the two tiers, and a process killed mid-migration reopens onto either
  the pre-archive or the complete post-archive topology -- never a half
  moved segment or copies left in both tiers;
* verification of long logs is incremental: unchanged byte windows are
  authenticated by an on-disk cache (stat-guarded on the active unit,
  window-material-guarded on sealed units), so a repeated verification of
  a ten-thousand-entry log only hashes newly appended bytes plus a small
  amount of sidecar material;
* tampering with the cache, the manifest or a sealed window is reported as
  chain corruption with the real first bad global index (never a pass, and
  distinct from the half-line bad-line semantics);
* ``export_range`` produces an offline proof for a contiguous index
  interval: only the interval's records plus the window anchors needed to
  attach the chain, verifiable with the public digest alone;
* ``recover`` is the explicit entry point that truncates a half-written
  tail line left by a killed process.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import hashlib
import os
from typing import Any, Optional

from . import record as rec
from . import storage as st

_ENCODING = "utf-8"
_FILE_UNIT = "$"
# os.open() defaults to text mode on Windows, which silently rewrites "\n"
# into "\r\n" (and re-translates bytes that already carry CRLF). The record
# format is defined byte for byte around a single "\n" terminator -- window
# sizes/hashes, byte offsets and folds all depend on that -- so every data
# fd must be opened binary. O_BINARY is absent (and therefore zero) on
# POSIX, where this changes nothing.
_O_BINARY = getattr(os, "O_BINARY", 0)
_DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT = 10.0
_DEFAULT_MAX_SEGMENTS = 2
# Present in the store directory while an archive migration is in flight;
# left behind only by a killed migration and cleared by the next healer.
_ARCHIVE_MARKER = ".archiving"


class Chain:
    """Append-only, per-tenant hash-chained audit log."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        path: str,
        *,
        lock_timeout: Optional[float] = _DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT,
    ):
        self.path = path
        self.lock_timeout = lock_timeout

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Layout / locking
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _lock_path(self) -> str:
        normalized = os.path.normpath(self.path)
        parent = os.path.dirname(normalized) or "."
        return os.path.join(parent, "." + os.path.basename(normalized) + ".lock")

    def _layout(self) -> st.Layout:
        existing = st.resolve_existing(self.path)
        if existing is not None:
            return existing
        # Nothing on disk yet: stay in the legacy file layout until the
        # first append (or an explicit rotate) creates anything.
        return st.Layout(self.path, "file")

    def _needs_adoption(self) -> bool:
        backup = self.path + ".pre-segment"
        return not os.path.exists(self.path) and os.path.exists(backup)

    @contextlib.contextmanager
    def _locked(self, *, exclusive: bool):
        # Readers open shared. A tree left mid-operation by a killed process
        # is not in a quiescent state (backup to adopt, staging dir, merge
        # temp file or an unreferenced segment); such a reader escalates
        # once to an exclusive lock, heals the tree deterministically, and
        # only then reads. In a quiescent tree no escalation happens, so the
        # ordinary read path stays shared.
        want_exclusive = exclusive or self._needs_adoption()
        while True:
            with st.file_lock(
                self._lock_path(), timeout=self.lock_timeout, shared=not want_exclusive
            ):
                if not want_exclusive:
                    layout = st.resolve_existing(self.path)
                    if layout is None:
                        layout = st.Layout(self.path, "file")
                    if self._needs_healing(layout):
                        want_exclusive = True
                        continue  # release the shared lock, re-enter exclusive
                    yield layout
                    return

                self._adopt_backup()
                layout = st.resolve_existing(self.path)
                if layout is None:
                    layout = st.Layout(self.path, "file")
                self._reap_crash_leftovers(layout)
                yield layout
                return

    def _needs_healing(self, layout: st.Layout) -> bool:
        """Whether a shared read must escalate to heal before reading.

        A read escalates when the live path is absent and a migration
        backup is waiting -- without adoption there is nothing to read --
        or when an archive migration marker is present: the marker means a
        migration was interrupted between its first manifest commit and its
        final cleanup, so the tree may physically straddle the two tiers
        (a hot duplicate of an archived segment, or a staged copy/temp in
        the archive directory) and must be settled onto exactly one
        topology before reading. Both checks are bare ``exists`` probes, so
        the ordinary read path pays no extra I/O. Every other leftover
        (staging directory, an unreferenced segment from a rotation or
        compaction killed before/after its manifest commit, a merge temp
        file, a post-publish backup) is inert while the committed manifest
        stays authoritative, so reads leave it untouched and the next
        writer (exclusive) reaps it -- matching the baseline rule that
        reads never move garbage out from under other readers.
        """
        if not os.path.exists(self.path) and os.path.exists(
            self.path + ".pre-segment"
        ):
            return True
        return layout.kind == "dir" and os.path.exists(
            os.path.join(layout.root, _ARCHIVE_MARKER)
        )

    def _reap_crash_leftovers(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
        """Deterministically finish every crash window's housekeeping."""
        backup = self.path + ".pre-segment"
        staging = self.path + ".segstage"
        if layout.kind == "file":
            # The store never happened: drop any staged directory and let
            # _adopt_backup move the file back.
            if os.path.isdir(staging):
                self._remove_tree(staging)
            return

        # The segment store is the published topology. A backup left behind
        # means the migration was killed right after publishing the store.
        if os.path.exists(backup):
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                os.remove(backup)
                st.fsync_dir(os.path.dirname(self.path) or ".")
        if os.path.isdir(staging):
            self._remove_tree(staging)

        manifest = None
        with contextlib.suppress(st.AuditMetadataError):
            manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
        if manifest is not None:
            self._gc_segments(layout, manifest)
            self._gc_archive(layout, manifest)
            # The migration is settled once the tiers agree with the
            # committed manifest; drop the in-flight marker so shared reads
            # stop escalating.
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                os.remove(os.path.join(layout.root, _ARCHIVE_MARKER))
                st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
        # Temp files of killed atomic writes/merges (never the lock).
        if os.path.isdir(layout.root):
            for name in os.listdir(layout.root):
                if name.startswith(".") and name.endswith(".tmp"):
                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                        os.remove(os.path.join(layout.root, name))
            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)

    @staticmethod
    def _remove_tree(path: str) -> None:
        import shutil

        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            shutil.rmtree(path)

    def _adopt_backup(self) -> None:
        """Restore a log left behind by a migration killed mid-rename.

        rotate() renames the legacy file aside before putting the segment
        store in its place; if the process is killed between the two renames,
        the file survives as a backup and is moved back on the next open.
        """
        backup = self.path + ".pre-segment"
        staging = self.path + ".segstage"
        if os.path.exists(self.path) or not os.path.exists(backup):
            return
        if os.path.isdir(staging):
            self._remove_tree(staging)
        parent = os.path.dirname(self.path) or "."
        os.replace(backup, self.path)
        st.fsync_dir(parent)

    def _view(self, layout: st.Layout) -> list[dict]:
        """Ordered units that make up the log, oldest first.

        A unit is the legacy single file or one manifest segment. Sealed
        units carry preserved byte windows (verification material); the
        active unit and the legacy file are fingerprinted as they grow.
        """
        if layout.kind == "file":
            return [
                {
                    "name": _FILE_UNIT,
                    "path": layout.root,
                    "sealed": False,
                    "parts": [],
                }
            ]

        manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
        if manifest is None:
            # Segment stores are created atomically (manifest + first
            # segment) by rotate(); a directory without one is a path
            # collision, never an implicit store.
            raise ValueError("missing audit manifest")

        return [
            {
                "name": segment["name"],
                "path": self._segment_path(layout, manifest, segment),
                "sealed": segment["sealed"],
                "parts": [dict(part) for part in segment["parts"]],
            }
            for segment in manifest["segments"]
        ]

    @staticmethod
    def _segment_path(layout: st.Layout, manifest: dict, segment: dict) -> str:
        """Where a manifest segment's bytes live: hot store or archive."""
        archive_dir = manifest.get("archive")
        if segment.get("archived") and archive_dir:
            return os.path.join(archive_dir, segment["name"])
        return layout.segment_path(segment["name"])

    def _raw_units(self, layout: st.Layout) -> list[dict]:
        """Units reconstructed from ordered segment file names alone.

        Used when the manifest cannot be trusted: the records themselves
        still carry the chain, so the real first bad index stays derivable.
        """
        if layout.kind == "file":
            return self._view(layout)
        names = sorted(
            name
            for name in os.listdir(layout.root)
            if st.seg_seq(name) is not None
        )
        return [
            {
                "name": name,
                "path": layout.segment_path(name),
                "sealed": False,
                "parts": [],
            }
            for name in names
        ]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Raw reads (entries/head; structure only, no chain or cache)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _all_records(self, units: list[dict], *, missing_empty: bool) -> list[dict]:
        records: list[dict] = []
        for unit in units:
            try:
                raw = st.scan_segment_bytes(unit["path"])
            except FileNotFoundError:
                if missing_empty and not unit["sealed"]:
                    continue
                raise
            records.extend(st.decode_records(raw))
        return records

    def _snapshot_units(
        self, layout: st.Layout, *, tolerate_metadata: bool
    ) -> list[dict]:
        try:
            return self._view(layout)
        except st.AuditMetadataError:
            if not tolerate_metadata:
                raise
            return self._raw_units(layout)

    def _tenant_records(self, tenant: str, *, missing_empty: bool) -> list[dict]:
        with self._locked(exclusive=False) as layout:
            if layout.kind == "file" and not os.path.exists(layout.root):
                if missing_empty:
                    return []
                raise FileNotFoundError(layout.root)
            # One fixed unit list and one ordered byte read under the shared
            # lock: writers (exclusive) cannot rotate, merge or recover
            # mid-call, so the result is always one complete prefix.
            units = self._snapshot_units(layout, tolerate_metadata=True)
            records = self._all_records(units, missing_empty=missing_empty)
        return [record for record in records if record["tenant"] == tenant]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public read API (unchanged shapes)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def entries(self, tenant: str) -> list[dict]:
        """Return all of the tenant's records in insertion order."""
        return self._tenant_records(tenant, missing_empty=True)

    def head(self, tenant: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """Return the tenant's newest digest, or None for an empty chain."""
        records = self._tenant_records(tenant, missing_empty=True)
        if not records:
            return None
        return records[-1]["digest"]

    def verify(self, tenant: str) -> dict:
        """Re-derive the tenant's chain, incrementally across segments.

        Returns ``{"count": n, "first_bad": i, "ok": bool}`` with global,
        zero-based per-tenant indices. Raises ``FileNotFoundError`` when the
        log is absent and ``ValueError`` on a bad or half-written line.
        Tampering with the cache, the manifest or a sealed window is itself
        corruption: the verdict is ``ok=False`` with the real first bad
        index rather than an exception.
        """
        metadata_damaged = False
        with self._locked(exclusive=False) as layout:
            self._require_present(layout)
            try:
                units = self._view(layout)
            except st.AuditMetadataError:
                # A rewritten manifest cannot vouch for any window: fall
                # back to the physically ordered segment files and re-derive
                # every link from the bytes themselves.
                metadata_damaged = True
                units = self._raw_units(layout)

            try:
                states, _ = self._walk(
                    units,
                    layout,
                    ignore_cache=metadata_damaged,
                    persist=not metadata_damaged,
                )
            except st.AuditMetadataError:
                # The sidecar cache was tampered with. It is neither trusted
                # nor silently healed: re-derive from bytes and report the
                # metadata damage as corruption below.
                metadata_damaged = True
                states, _ = self._walk(units, layout, ignore_cache=True, persist=False)

        state = states.get(tenant)
        if state is None:
            return {"count": 0, "first_bad": -1, "ok": True}
        count, _head, bad = state
        if bad != -1:
            # The byte-level walk found the real break first; it always
            # outranks the metadata tripwire.
            return {"count": count, "first_bad": bad, "ok": False}
        if metadata_damaged:
            # The bytes still re-derive, but authentication material the
            # chain depended on (manifest windows or the verified cache) was
            # rewritten: the earliest index it could vouch for is 0.
            return {"count": count, "first_bad": 0, "ok": False}
        return {"count": count, "first_bad": -1, "ok": True}

    def _require_present(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
        if layout.kind == "file":
            if not os.path.isfile(layout.root):
                raise FileNotFoundError(layout.root)
            return
        # An existing directory without a manifest is malformed; let the
        # view report it rather than masking it as a missing file.
        if not os.path.isdir(layout.root):
            raise FileNotFoundError(layout.root)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Append
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def append(self, tenant: str, payload: Any) -> dict:
        """Append one record for ``tenant`` and return the stored entry.

        Raises ``TypeError`` for a non-object payload and ``ValueError`` if
        the existing log, its cache or its manifest is corrupt; existing
        records are left untouched. Concurrent appenders are serialized by
        a file lock.
        """
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise TypeError("payload must be a dict")

        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
            units = self._view(layout)

            # Refuse to extend a damaged log.
            states, entries = self._walk(units, layout)
            for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
                if bad != -1:
                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")

            prev = states.get(tenant, (0, "", -1))[1]
            record, line = rec.build_line(tenant, payload, prev)
            target = units[-1]["path"]
            data = (line + "\n").encode(_ENCODING)
            # Two raw writes with a real kill point between them model the
            # write/flush/fsync crash window: a kill after the first syscall
            # leaves a deterministic half line that reopen treats as a bad
            # line, never as a silently repaired record.
            cut = max(1, len(data) // 2)
            fd = os.open(
                target, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | _O_BINARY, 0o600
            )
            try:
                _write_all(fd, data[:cut])
                st.crash_point("append:after_first_write")
                _write_all(fd, data[cut:])
                st.crash_point("append:before_fsync")
                os.fsync(fd)
                st.crash_point("append:after_fsync")
            finally:
                os.close(fd)

            # Warm the cache with the single record just written: suffix
            # only, never a rehash of the whole file. The continuation is
            # computed from the entries this same locked section
